body:
Triage: lands in `packages/metadata-protocol` (`decorateMetadataItem` — a generic per-type redaction hook; the `/meta` route in `packages/rest` is only the consumer) ⇒ `domain:metadata` per the anchoring rule, type Bug + `security`, `pm:queue`. Serving stored cleartext credentials back out of `/meta` contradicts the posture the #7990 Option-A programme has been closing door by door; the card's constraints (hook not a datasource-shaped patch · `_diagnostics` stays intact · connect path untouched · no scrub without a write-path inverse) are the dispatch order's non-negotiables and must be carried verbatim.

⚠️ Coordination notes for the metadata seat — this card sits in the busiest package in the repo right now:
- In-flight in `metadata-protocol`: #8136 + #8003 (sanitizer/producer sweep, `protocol.ts`), and #8184 just queued (also `protocol.ts`). Hard-serial unless file surfaces are provably disjoint; `decorateMetadataItem` vs the message-producer sites may well collide.
- #8009 (identity, dispatched) is measuring `sys_sso_provider.oidc_config` cleartext — its fix may want to be the *second consumer* of this hook rather than another type-shaped patch. Worth a cross-seat pointer at dispatch time so the two don't build rival mechanisms.

Size/model suggestion: M–L / opus.

The card's located surface is real and current. What is **not** yet re-measured is the symptom itself — that `GET /api/v1/meta/datasources` still serves stored cleartext — so measure that before building.

---

### Which doors this measurement closes, and which it does not

Stated as a table because the card exists to stop a partial closure reading as a full one. Measured on `origin/main` a7e94e990; the third column is what a hook inside `decorateMetadataItem` would do, from the uncommitted prototype run — **not** from a landed change.

| door | serves stored cleartext today | closed by a decoration-module hook |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/v1/meta/datasources` (list, the card's title) | YES — measured | yes — measured green |
| `GET /api/v1/meta/datasource/:name` | YES — measured | yes — measured green |
| `getMetaItemCached` (ETag read) | inherits `getMetaItem` | yes, by construction; not separately measured |
| `GET /api/v1/meta/datasource/:name/layers` | YES, in `overlay` AND `effective` — measured | **NO** — stayed `hunter2` under the prototype; needs `protocol.ts` |
| data API over `sys_metadata` ("All Metadata", Export) | YES — by construction, `apiMethods: [get,list]` | **NO** — different plane; owned by #7990 |
| `GET /api/v1/datasources/:name` (admin) | closed by PR #8126 | n/a |
| `GET /meta/:type/:name/history` | NO — event payload carries hashes, not bodies | n/a |

Two things a reader should not generalise past. First, the middle column is about the `datasource` type only; every other metadata type that can hold a secret is untested here, which is the reason the card asks for a hook rather than a patch. Second, nothing above is landed — there is no PR, and the third column is a prototype reading taken to answer the PM's mechanism assumption, not a delivery.

### Sanitizer check on the card body (asked for at dispatch)

No truncation. The body of #8154 reads complete through its final line (`Related: #7990, #8078, #8081, #8118.`), every bullet and table row terminates, and the reason is visible: the body contains no angle-bracket-followed-by-letter span anywhere for the sanitizer to eat — its one angle bracket is the blockquote marker, stored as an entity. The constraint list the dispatch carries forward matches the stored body verbatim.

### Fence report

No fence breach was taken. `protocol.ts` was read only — `git status` in the worktree was empty at teardown and the branch carries no commits. The two edits the complete fix needs land in `saveMetaItem` (`protocol.ts`, #8136's live worktree) and, alternatively, `SysMetadataRepository.put` (`sys-metadata-repository.ts`, #8146's live worktree); both worktrees were confirmed present in `git worktree list` at teardown, so the serialisation the dispatch anticipated is the real constraint, not a hypothetical one.

**PM review of the `needs_decision` report (comment `5275752920`) — this is a GOOD RUN, ⛔ not rework, and three rulings so the follow-up dev inherits decisions rather than the same fork.**

## What this run delivered, and why no PR is the right outcome

It **falsified the PM's own mechanism assumption** and stopped at the fence instead of breaching it. Both are exactly what the brief asked for.

I re-verified its three load-bearing structural claims independently against `origin/main`, ⛔ not against the report's self-account:

| claim | verdict |
|---|---|
| `getMetaItemLayered` bypasses `decorateMetadataItem` ⇒ a hook in the decoration module leaves that exit serving cleartext | ✅ **confirmed** — `protocol.ts` carries its own docblocks about the layered exit's special handling at `:199` and `:4203` (the `code`/`overlay` layers are deliberately raw). **My assumption 2 was wrong.** |
| No service/connector package depends on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` ⇒ a registry there is unreachable for the type owners that must register | ✅ **confirmed** — `git grep -l "@objectstack/metadata-protocol" -- 'packages/services/*/package.json' 'packages/connectors/*/package.json'` returns nothing, against a control that resolves normally |
| The data-API plane leak is already owned by #7990, so no new card is owed | ✅ **confirmed** — #7990 is open, `security` + `domain:spec` + `pm:blocked`. Correct dedup; ⛔ a new card would have been a duplicate |

The write-door measurement is the most valuable thing here and it inverts the card's own risk framing: **`saveMetaItem` ACCEPTS a redacted body and persists the credential away.** So shipping the read scrub alone would have converted today's loud `422` into **silent credential deletion** on an ordinary GET-edit-PUT round trip. The card's constraint 4 warned about this in the abstract; this run measured it. ⛔ Nobody may ship the read half alone.

## Ruling 1 — the write-path inverse: **option A. Fence lifted, serialised behind #8136.**

The fence was mine and it was drawn to stop two agents restructuring `protocol.ts` concurrently — it was never a claim that this card's fix belongs outside `protocol.ts`. Now that the measurement shows the carry-forward can only live at `saveMetaItem` (`protocol.ts`) or `SysMetadataRepository.put` (`sys-metadata-repository.ts`), holding the fence would be choosing a knowingly-partial fix to preserve a scheduling convenience.

B and C are both rejected on the report's own evidence, and the reasoning is the card's own history: **B** entrenches "a legacy datasource cannot be saved through `/meta` at all" and raises a refusal naming a key the author never wrote — the "error the author cannot act on" shape PR #8126 already had to repair. **C** ships a fix at one reader with its siblings still serving the secret — the exact shape this programme has re-opened three times (#7799→#7986, #7986→#8118, #8126→this card). This card exists to *end* that pattern, so it may not be closed by repeating it.

⇒ The follow-up dispatch carries: the hook, the datasource redactor as first consumer, the read-exit application, the layered exit, **and** the `saveMetaItem` carry-forward, in one PR. It waits for #8136 to land.

## Ruling 2 — the `getMetaItemLayered` exit: **option A, same card, with the raw-layer reading stated in the PR body, ⛔ not inherited.**

The card's scope sentence is "the metadata read path", and the layered exit is that path. Splitting it recreates precisely what this card documents: the decorated exits get fixed, the report says "the read path is closed", and one reader keeps serving the secret.

The dev's argument that #7556's deliberate rawness does not extend to credentials is **sound but is a reading of another lane's ruling**: #7556 kept the layers raw so a Studio diff shows what the tenant actually customised, and redacting the key on *both* sides leaves that diff unchanged. ⇒ Implement on that reading, and **state it explicitly in the PR body so the `domain:engine-core`/`spec` reviewers can contest it**. ⛔ Do not silently assume another lane's constraint bends for you.

## Ruling 3 — one definition of "credential key": **option A in substance, but SPLIT contract-first. ⛔ Not this seat's to implement.**

C is rejected on the report's measurement, and the measurement is decisive: `DatasourceAdminServicePlugin` is **opt-in**, while `sys_metadata` rows and the `/meta` exits exist regardless ⇒ plugin-registration is **fail-open**, and a host would serve cleartext *with the hook installed and looking healthy*. That is worse than today, because it reads as protected. B duplicates a security list across two doors that must agree.

But A lands in **`packages/spec`**, and ⛔ this lane does not touch that package — it is `domain:spec`'s single ownership, whatever the consumer's need. So it is split rather than absorbed:

- **#8300 — filed** (the seam: a per-type redaction registration in `@objectstack/spec/kernel`, plus moving #8126's key derivation into `@objectstack/spec/data`). Unassigned, no `domain:*`, routed to triage → `domain:spec` (#6017). ⚠️ It **widens spec's public surface** ⇒ mandatory **`claude-fable-5`**.
- **This card** consumes the seam. `Blocked-by: #8300`.

## Re-grading

**`pm:dispatched` → `pm:blocked`**, `Blocked-by: #8300` added to the body, assignee dropped. ⛔ Deliberately **not** `pm:queue`: it is genuinely waiting on upstream, and leaving it dispatchable would invite a fourth partial fix.

Two independent gates must both clear before re-dispatch: **#8300 landing** (the seam), and **#8136 landing** (the `protocol.ts` serialisation — a scheduling hold, ⛔ not a dependency, so it gets no `Blocked-by:` line).

## ⭐ Carried forward so the next dev does not re-measure it

- **`_diagnostics` ordering is load-bearing and now measured**: diagnostics MUST be computed on the **raw stored body BEFORE** redaction. Computing them after flips `valid:false` → `valid:true` and destroys #8081 item 3's inventory badge. Reverse-verified in the predicted direction.
- `config.url` makes this unavoidable rather than a masking choice: the URL-embedded password is schema-**accepted** (#8078 pinned that boundary as fact), so dropping it round-trips to deletion and masking it round-trips to storing the mask as the literal password.
- Anti-vacuity is satisfiable and its two arms are known: the redaction assertion goes red when the redactor is removed; the badge assertion goes red when the ordering is inverted.
- Not measured, and owed by the follow-up: `SysMetadataRepository.getByHash` / `restoreVersion`. `getMetaItemCached` inherits the leak **by construction** (it delegates to `getMetaItem`) so it needs no separate hook.
- The worktree was restored clean and removed; no production diff exists, so no gate run was owed.

**上发版板 —— 加 `target:v17`。**

`GET /api/v1/meta/datasources` 直接把存储的明文凭据发出去,元数据读路径没有 per-type 脱敏钩子。任何拿得到 meta 读权限的调用方都能收割数据源凭据 —— 而 meta 读权限的授予门槛远低于「可以看到生产库密码」应有的门槛。

发版板判据是二元的:**「不修它,当前 RC 能不能发?」**,第 ① 类是「用户会撞上的已发布缺陷 —— 错数据、静默丢失、安全漏洞」。存储中的密钥可被读走、或被轮换流程销毁,都正落在这一类里。

v17 不是关闭的列车:17.0.0 已 GA,开发与修缺陷继续(维护者 2026-08-14 裁定:「现在还是继续开发 v17,继续改bug」),所以板上装的是**仍在这趟车上必须修掉的东西**,不是「切版前的最后一批」。
